C08-M08-L06-F1.title: CASE-0001 reconstructed: attacker and SOC on one clock
C08-M08-L06-F1.caption: Dataset events for WS-104, the beacon and the VPN spray on a 06:00-08:40 UTC axis, with the illustrative SOC times, showing that the whole intrusion ran before anyone noticed.
C08-M08-L06-F1.alt: Timeline with four rows on an axis from 06:00 to 08:40 UTC. Red row, WS-104 attacker actions: six ticks at 06:12 download, 06:14 PowerShell, 07:02 and 07:03 svc_update, 08:12 upload and 08:17 log cleared. Orange row, beacon to cdn-telemetry-sync.example: 18 evenly spaced ticks from 06:17 to 07:42, 220 bytes every 300 seconds. Violet row, VPN spray and gopal login: eight ticks packed at 06:42 and one at 06:46. Green row, SOC response, illustrative: ticks at 08:25 noticed and 08:31 IR lead acknowledgement. Note: dwell time 133 minutes from first malicious event to time noticed.
C08-M08-L06-F1.note: Dwell time 133 min from first malicious event (06:12) to time noticed (08:25); every attacker action came first.

C08-M08-L06-F2.title: Root cause and contributing factors for CASE-0001
C08-M08-L06-F2.caption: The causal factors the Banyan review found, each tied to dataset evidence, feeding the incident outcome.
C08-M08-L06-F2.alt: Tree with arrows pointing into the root. Root, dark: Outcome: data likely taken, log cleared (48.2 MB upload 08:12, 1102 at 08:17). Six children feed it. Red: Root cause: macro document ran PowerShell (internet .docm on a payments approver host). Orange: Look-alike domain reachable (banyan-payroll-update.example, status 200). Orange: Session could create a local admin (4720 and 4732 under divya's session). Violet: R1 matched at 06:14, noticed 08:25 (detection-to-response gap). Violet: Beacon ranked last in the queue (R6 priority 3.6). Orange: Upload to never-seen domain allowed (files-share-drop.example, status 200).
